subject.title: Feature Request: Automated Session Memory Preservation & Synthesis

question: Should OpenClaw core own structured session-memory synthesis and startup hydration, or should core only expose lifecycle hooks while plugins/MCP packages own this behavior?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent design affects silent model calls, transcript retention, startup context, plugin boundaries, and config/security defaults, so automation should not choose the policy alone.

options.title: Define a bounded core contract
options.body: Approve a narrow core design for reset/session-start memory continuity with opt-in synthesis, timeout, redaction, dedupe, and clear docs before implementation.

options.title: Route synthesis to plugins or MCP
options.body: Keep core limited to generic lifecycle hooks and document existing plugin/MCP approaches such as world-model-mcp for richer memory synthesis.

options.title: Split and close later
options.body: Track trigger expansion in #15828 and pre-reset agentic flush in #45608, then close this issue only after the startup synthesis and transcript-linking decision is explicitly assigned or rejected.

recommendation.title: Define a bounded core contract
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow core design for reset/session-start memory continuity with opt-in synthesis, timeout, redaction, dedupe, and clear docs before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has history on both `/new` reset behavior and the pre-compaction memory flush primitive, making them the best available owner for the cross-boundary product/security decision.
